title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
statement: A path is any connected sequence of nodes moving along parent-child links (no node twice); it need not pass through the root or end at a leaf. Return the maximum sum of node values over all non-empty paths. The tree has at least one node.

hints.1_question: At each node, a best path 'turns' there: it goes down into at most one child on each side. What should you do with a child whose best downward path is negative?
hints.2_nudge: Compute, bottom-up, the best downward gain from each node. A path through a node = node + max(0, left gain) + max(0, right gain). Track the global best, but return only one side upward.
hints.3_big_hint: g(n) = n.val + max(0, g(left), g(right)) for the upward return; best = max(best, n.val + max(0, g(left)) + max(0, g(right))).

known_bugs.name: does not drop negative child gains
known_bugs.followup: If a subtree's best downward path sums to a negative number, is it worth including?

known_bugs.name: best starts at 0 (never reports a negative answer)
known_bugs.followup: The path must contain at least one node. What is the answer for a tree whose every value is negative?

known_bugs.name: only considers the path through the root
known_bugs.followup: Could the best path live entirely inside one subtree and avoid the root?

followups: Why do you return only one child's gain to the parent?
How is this related to the tree diameter?
